history.idea:
Replace the random-order baseline with a filter + dedupe + in-domain-only selection:

1. Format gate. Keep a doc only if it looks like the target (WikiText style): the first line matches `^= .+ =$`, or it has at least 3 of the WikiText tokenisation markers per 1000 characters (' @-@ ', ' @,@ ', ' @.@ ', ' , ', ' . ', ' ( ').

2. Damage filter for shuffled-word docs. Build the set of lowercase whitespace-word bigrams from target_sample. For each candidate, compute the fraction of its bigrams (first ~600 words after the title line) that are in that set. Compute the same statistic leave-one-out on the target docs, and set the threshold at (5th percentile of target scores) * 0.8. Drop docs below it; shuffled docs such as the 'Pulaski Skyway' one should score far lower.

3. Junk filter. Drop docs with fewer than 200 characters, docs where len(zlib.compress(text)) / len(text) < 0.2 (repeated boilerplate), and docs with more than 30% non-alphabetic, non-space characters.

4. Dedupe. Drop exact duplicates by hash of the whitespace-normalised lowercase text, and near-duplicates by keeping only one doc per (title line, first 200 normalised characters) key, preferring the longest.

5. Order and fill. Shuffle the survivors with random.Random(CURATE_SEED). Count tokens with tiktoken gpt2 (or estimate chars/4 if time is tight). If survivors total at least 0.5 T tokens, return just them and let the trainer cycle. Otherwise append the remaining non-junk, deduped, non-shuffled out-of-domain docs, ranked by bigram-hit fraction, until the total reaches T, then shuffle the whole list.
history.outcome: dev 1.9376 against 1.9617 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best
